newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: WorldSpace gives Japanese firms digital radio deals.
newsitem.headline: WorldSpace gives Japanese firms digital radio deals.

text.p: Satellite radio broadcasting company WorldSpace Inc said on Tuesday it had awarded contracts to four Japanese electronics companies to manufacture a new generation of digital radio receivers.
WorldSpace chairman Noah Samara told Reuters the four companies were Hitachi Ltd, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd (Panasonic), a subsidiary of Sanyo Electric Co Ltd and JVC ltd.

Samara said the four companies would have the exclusive right for three years from 1998 to make 30-45 million new radio sets to receive broadcasts from WorldSpace's new system, the world's first satellite radio network.
He said in an interview the four Japanese companies would announce the contracts formally in Singapore at 0800 GMT.
Samara said it was difficult to give an estimate of the financial value of the contracts, but that they were very valuable.
"If everyone had the same market share, it is a project that has a potential of literally hundreds of millions of U.S. dollars for each of these manaufacturers," he said.
